subject: MSA — Sequence for Customer Defense, Notice Timing & Escrow Threshold
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@northgate.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@northgate.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA: Indemnity — proposed customer defense/notice process

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking a look at our MSA redlines (attached). A couple of high-level items from our counsel:

- We're asking for language that gives Northgate the right to assume control of the defense for third-party IP claims (so we can manage PR and technical remediation quickly).
- If Northgate assumes defense, Redwood must pay reasonable defense costs and any settlement amounts; Redwood should have the opportunity to participate.
- Timing: we need a short notice/cure window to surface claims and decide on indemnity — proposing 10 business days after notice for Redwood to respond/accept.
- Escrow/holdback: our procurement team wants a fall-back that allows an escrow or holdback for large IP exposure; they proposed a $250k threshold.

We can be flexible on mutual cooperation obligations, but our counsel wants clarity on who controls counsel selection, where litigation happens, and how costs above the escrow are allocated.

Attaching our redline for your legal team's review: Northgate_MSA_redlines_20261130.pdf

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on: (1) customer control of defense, (2) cure/notice timing, and (3) any escrow/threshold guardrails?

Best,
Sarah Lin
Head of Legal Operations
Northgate Analytics

--

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA: Indemnity — proposed customer defense/notice process

Sarah — thanks for the clear redline and callout bullets. I've summarized Redwood's high-level stance below and attached a short response workbook.

High-level Redwood positions:
- Redwood will indemnify and defend for third-party IP claims to the extent they arise from Redwood's Service (not Customer modifications or Customer-provided content).
- Redwood prefers to retain the right to control the defense, including counsel selection, to ensure consistent claim strategy and avoid conflicting defenses. That said, we are open to Customer assuming defense in limited circumstances if Redwood can appoint local co-counsel and approve any settlement that imposes obligations on Redwood.
- Notice/cure window: our standard is prompt written notice and 30 days to accept or cure; we are willing to discuss shortening to 14 days for particularly time-sensitive claims, but 10 business days is aggressive for initial evaluation.
- Escrow/holdback: Redwood does not typically agree to a customer-controlled escrow for indemnity without a clear trigger. If Customer insists on a holdback, we should seek a $500k threshold (or a defined percentage of the committed spend) and narrow the trigger to final, adjudicated liabilities or a settlement we have consented to.

Next steps: can your counsel confirm whether Northgate requires unilateral customer control of counsel selection or whether Northgate would accept joint-selection with an agreed panel? If they need a $250k escrow floor, we'll need procurement to justify the lower threshold.

I'll loop Legal for guidance on control language and propose some compromise markup. Attaching: redwood_response_summary_20261202.xlsx

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA: Indemnity — proposed customer defense/notice process

Team — quick internal guidance for negotiation strategy (thread for reference):

1) Defense control: push for Redwood control of defense with right to appoint counsel and control settlement decisions that bind Redwood. We can offer Customer the ability to assume defense provided Redwood can (a) step in at its option, (b) approve counsel, and (c) veto settlements that affect Redwood.

2) Notice and cure: counter-propose 21 calendar days for Redwood to respond/accept or initiate negotiations, with an Uber-fast escalation path for claims that risk immediate injunctions (48–72 hours to provide preliminary position/ready an interim response). Avoid 10 business days — operationally risky.

3) Escrow/holdback threshold: don't agree to $250k. Push for $500k or a clear, proven indemnifiable liability (e.g., final adjudication or settlement). If Customer insists, require: (i) escrow duration capped at 12 months post-claim; (ii) mutual set-off rights; (iii) escrow release triggers clearly defined.

4) Exclusions: ensure carveouts for claims arising from (i) Customer's modifications, (ii) Customer data that causes infringement, and (iii) open-source components (limited to bona fide licenses).

5) Litigation venue & counsel selection: prefer courts in Redwood's domicile (CA), but offer Customer reciprocal forum selection rights for its local jurisdictions for injunctive relief requests.

If you need me to take point on a redline, I can draft language tonight. Otherwise I recommend we push back on the escrow floor and offer joint counsel-selection language with veto/approval rights.

-Rishi
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA: Indemnity — proposed customer defense/notice process

Sarah — thanks again for the redline. After internal review, Redwood can accept the following compromise to move the deal forward:

- Defense control: Redwood will generally control the defense for covered third-party IP claims. Customer may assume defense only where Redwood chooses not to (and subject to Redwood's right to step in). If Customer assumes defense, Redwood will pay reasonable defense costs and will have approval rights over any settlement that binds Redwood. Counsel selection: joint selection from an agreed panel; if the parties cannot agree, Redwood shall appoint counsel for matters affecting Redwood.

- Notice & timing: Customer must provide prompt written notice. Redwood will have 21 calendar days to accept defense or notify of intent to step in. For potential injunctions or urgent threats, Redwood will provide a preliminary position within 72 hours of notice.

- Escrow/holdback: Redwood cannot agree to an unconditional $250k escrow. We will accept a $500k threshold tied to final settlement/adjudication or a documented settlement amount the parties consent to. Escrow duration limited to 12 months following placement; release mechanics to be defined in the Order Form.

- Exclusions: carveouts remain for Customer modifications, Customer-provided data that causes infringement, and certain open-source claims.

Next steps: I've prepared a clean markup that implements the compromise — please review and confirm whether Northgate can accept the $500k threshold. If yes, we'll circulate the redline via DocuSign and schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call early next week to finalize.
